heading: IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

REGIONAL GAZETTE

NUMBER 2 YEAR 2013

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUDUS REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the power of the Government of the State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is Kudus Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regent is the Regent of Kudus.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kudus Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit in charge of women's empowerment and child protection.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the SKPD in charge.
12. Violence is any form of unlawful act that may result in or cause danger to a person whether physical, sexual, psychological and economic in nature.
13. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
14. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Psychological Violence or psychic violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
18. Economic Violence is any act that may be in the form of restricting a person's right to work decently inside or outside the home and also acts of neglecting family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
19. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who because of their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
20. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment both physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
21. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
23. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, medicolegal services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
24. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims.
25. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with specified operational standards.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

Integrated Services

heading: Article 6
translated_text:
Article 6

In providing protection to victims of gender-based violence and child victims of violence, the Regional Government is assisted by Integrated Services.

heading: Article 7
Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

Further provisions regarding the establishment of Integrated Services shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Prevention Efforts

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

Prevention efforts as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (3) letter a include:
a. conducting communication, information, and education about gender-based violence and violence against children; and
b. socialization of laws and regulations related to gender-based violence and violence against children.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Recovery and Social Reintegration Efforts

heading: Article 10
Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Legal Protection

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

Legal protection as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (3) letter c includes:
a. providing assistance during the legal process at every stage of examination; and
b. providing special legal protection for child victims of violence which may be carried out through the appointment of guardianship in accordance with applicable regulations.

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Coordination and Cooperation

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

Coordination and cooperation as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (3) letter d include:
a. coordinating and cooperating in handling cases of violence with integrated services at the regency/city level;
b. coordinating and cooperating with service provider institutions for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children; and
c. coordinating and consulting with the Regional Government.

heading: Part Six
translated_text:
Part Six

Increasing Community Participation

heading: Article 13
Part Seven
translated_text:
Part Seven

Monitoring and Reporting

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (3) letter f shall be conducted on all aspects of integrated service activities in the form of supervision, documentation and evaluation of cases of gender-based violence and violence against children.

heading: Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

The implementation of Integrated Services shall be coordinated by the relevant SKPD.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

ASSISTANCE

Article 16

Assistance shall be provided by persons or official institutions that have professional competence in their field and cooperate with Integrated Services.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

COOPERATION

Article 17

1. In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government, Provincial Government, and Regency/City Government, and other institutions.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government and Provincial Government as referred to in paragraph (1) includes consultation, coordination and reporting.
3. Cooperation between the Regional Government and Regency/City as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, facilitation of integrated service system development, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 18

1. Control, guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be carried out by the Regent.
2. The implementation of control, guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be assisted by the relevant SKPD.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

FINANCING

Article 19

All activities related to the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and other lawful and non-binding sources.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 20

Matters not yet regulated in this Regional Regulation insofar as they concern implementation shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Kudus Regency.

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUDUS REGENCY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUDUS REGENCY

NUMBER 2 OF 2014 CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUDUS REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Women and children have an important role in the development of a nation. Women as mothers of the nation who will give birth to children and children as the next generation of the nation are capital for national development that need to obtain legal protection from acts of gender-based violence and violence against children.

Gender-based violence and violence against children are currently increasing in number. Several forms of acts of violence against women and children that occur in society can be in the form of social harassment, rape, trafficking of women and children, pornography, sexual exploitation, neglect, domestic violence. Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection of the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.

In order to realize the protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as referred to above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children.

heading: Article 2
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUDUS REGENCY
translated_text:
Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and violence against children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b
What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c
What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.

What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, aligned and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d
What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e
What is meant by "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, covering the right to identity.

What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, covering the right to create and recreate.

Letter f
What is meant by "respect for the child's opinion" is respect for the rights of children to participate and express their opinions in decision-making that can be taken into consideration, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter g
What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children it is transparent among integrated service providers.

Letter h
What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children it is carried out by building coordination between service providers, including medical services, legal assistance, psychologists, religious counselors, social workers, police.

Letter i
What is meant by "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.

Letter j
What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.
